title: Pre-US pullback: overnight high given back before the US open, is it retaken at US start? (BTCUSDT 1m)

what.name: Giveback
what.value_plain: (overnight high - price at 13:00 UTC) / overnight range; event = high made after 03:00 UTC and giveback >= 0.5; strong = >= 0.8
what.label: OURS

what.name: US window
what.value_plain: 13:00-20:00 UTC; which is hit first, the overnight high or the overnight low
what.label: OURS

what.name: Costs
what.value_plain: none: a base rate (what happens next), not a trade
what.label: OURS

how: preus_pullback.py reads every BTCUSDT 1m day 2022-01..2026-09 (1730 days) and counts which overnight extreme the US session takes first. Base rate only, no entries, no fees.
window: 2022-01-01 to 2026-09-30 (whole history read: a base rate, not a sealed test)

verdict.label: Strong giveback (>= 0.8): overnight low taken first 85 %, high retaken first 6 % (n 84). All days: 41 % / 42 %.

why: On the 84 days where price gave back 80 % or more of the overnight range by 13:00 UTC, the US session took the overnight low first on 85 % and retook the high first on only 6 %.
On all 1730 days the split is near even (high first 42 %, low first 41 %), so the giveback, not the clock, carries the information.
Not a trade test: no entry, stop or fee. Turning it into a short needs its own pre-registered backtest with fees.
